primary_gt.mechanism_question: separate cumulative heat stress from a single peak-temperature story by combining thermal load, persistence, recovery, and contextual evidence

computed_evidence.process_alignment_proof: The persistent heat-load rule passes: 43.4 C-day is above the 40 C-day diagnostic gate, 26 event-window days reached at least 40 C, and the longest hot run lasted 9 days. The hottest 3-day Tmax mean was 44.57 C from 2022-05-11 to 2022-05-13, showing an acute phase embedded in a longer hot period. The 0.118 warm-night ratio and 42.8 C peak apparent temperature add recovery and body-stress context without replacing the dry-bulb persistence test.
computed_evidence.computed_interpretation: The strongest computed diagnosis is sustained early-season heat-load accumulation with a mid-May peak, not a single-day diagnostic gate crossing.

primary_gt.decisive_evidence: Accumulated heat load, duration, and exposure scaling carry the mechanism decision; rainfall or image signals only test competing explanations.
primary_gt.rejected_simplifications: Reject peak-only, rainfall-led, and image-primary explanations when the computed heat-load chain is stronger.
primary_gt.bounded_interpretation: The result is a package-scale heat mechanism diagnosis, not exact mortality, outage, damage, or full regional attribution.
primary_gt.formula_derivation: Derive heat load as sum(max(T - T_ref, 0)); if exposure is used, scale it as heat_load * exposed_population / 100000 and explain the units.

event.location: North India and Pakistan heatwave corridor

decision_rule.summary: A high-quality answer computes the heat-load rule values and proves that the persistent early-season heat-load diagnosis passes all required inequalities.

incomplete_mechanisms.label: single_peak_heat_only
incomplete_mechanisms.why_rejected: The 45.3 C peak is important, but 26 days at or above 40 C and repeated 9-day hot runs show cumulative load.

incomplete_mechanisms.label: apparent_temperature_only_gate
incomplete_mechanisms.why_rejected: The 42.8 C apparent-temperature peak is body-relevant context, not a substitute for dry-bulb persistence and warm-night recovery.

incomplete_mechanisms.label: precipitation_or_remote_sensing_footprint_as_primary_mechanism
incomplete_mechanisms.why_rejected: Rainfall and surface-change context do not measure the main heat-health stress process.

incomplete_mechanisms.label: attribution_or_exposure_context_as_primary_diagnosis
incomplete_mechanisms.why_rejected: Attribution and exposure affect risk framing, but they do not replace persistence, recovery, and heat-load metrics.

criteria.name: mechanism_diagnosis
criteria.description: Identifies the dominant physical process and gives the correct compact mechanism label or equivalent diagnosis.

criteria.name: computed_evidence
criteria.description: Recomputes the package-derived quantitative evidence with correct units, signs, ratios, dates, and rounding.

criteria.name: formula_derivation
criteria.description: Shows the requested physical formula, scaling relation, or timing relation and connects it to the computed values.

criteria.name: evidence_weighting
criteria.description: Explains which evidence streams are decisive and which are contextual or weaker proxies.

criteria.name: counterfactual_rejection
criteria.description: Rejects tempting simplified explanations using computed values rather than assertion.

criteria.name: bounded_interpretation
criteria.description: States scale, timing, proxy, or uncertainty limits without adding unsupported losses or impacts.

criteria.name: json_contract
criteria.description: Returns the requested structured mechanism-diagnosis JSON without reducing the answer to a row-only table.
